profile.address: ul. Kazimierza Kaminskiego 6, 05-850 Ozarow Mazowiecki, Poland
profile.reading: This is OVHclouds WAW1 data center at ul. Kazimierza Kaminskiego 6 in Ozarow Mazowiecki, just west of Warsaw, Poland, a retrofitted building per third party data center directories. A directory listing places the facility as operational since 2016, though this registry could not independently corroborate that date against a primary OVH source this session, so it is carried with that caveat. OVHcloud does not publicly disclose power capacity or floor area figures for this specific site in any directory checked this session. OVH itself was founded in 1999 by Octave Klaba, then an engineering student in Lille, France, to meet growing demand for internet hosting, establishing its headquarters and first company owned data centers in Roubaix, France in 2004, the same year it opened a Polish subsidiary, making Poland one of OVHs earliest international markets. The Klaba family, Octave along with his parents Henryk and Halina and brother Miroslaw, retained majority ownership of the company even after US private equity firm KKR and TowerBrook Capital Partners acquired a minority stake in 2016, and the company rebranded from OVH to OVHcloud in 2019. OVHcloud describes itself today as Europes leading cloud provider, reporting more than 400,000 servers spread across upward of 46 data centers on four continents, serving more than 1.6 million customers across some 140 countries, a global footprint into which this Ozarow Mazowiecki facility fits as part of the companys Central European presence. OVH listed publicly for the first time in October 2021, debuting on Euronext Paris under the OVHcloud name with its shares closing the first trading day up about 6.5 percent and the company valued at roughly 4.3 billion dollars, a milestone in the companys transition from a privately held French hosting firm into a publicly traded European cloud provider while the Klaba family retained a controlling stake.
